result.label: Source-read

claims.claim: The federal text reported is from the 2024 edition of the United States Code.
Section 1692g(a) generally requires a collector to send written notice within five days after the initial communication with a consumer in connection with collecting a debt.
claims.quote: (a) Notice of debt; contents Within five days after the initial communication with a consumer in connection with the collection of any debt, a debt collector shall, unless the following information is contained in the initial communication or the consumer has paid the debt, send the consumer a written notice containing—

claims.claim: No separate notice is required if the initial communication contains the required information.
claims.quote: unless the following information is contained in the initial communication

claims.claim: No separate notice is required if the consumer has paid the debt.
claims.quote: unless the following information is contained in the initial communication or the consumer has paid the debt

claims.claim: The notice must give the amount of the debt.
The notice must name the creditor to whom the debt is owed.
claims.quote: (2) the name of the creditor to whom the debt is owed;

claims.claim: The notice must state that the collector will assume the debt is valid unless the consumer disputes its validity, in whole or in part, within thirty days after receipt of the notice.
claims.quote: (3) a statement that unless the consumer, within thirty days after receipt of the notice, disputes the validity of the debt, or any portion thereof, the debt will be assumed to be valid by the debt collector;

claims.claim: The notice must state that a written dispute of all or part of the debt within the thirty-day period requires the collector to obtain verification or a copy of a judgment against the consumer and mail a copy to the consumer.
claims.quote: (4) a statement that if the consumer notifies the debt collector in writing within the thirty-day period that the debt, or any portion thereof, is disputed, the debt collector will obtain verification of the debt or a copy of a judgment against the consumer and a copy of such verification or judgment will be mailed to the consumer by the debt collector;

claims.claim: The notice must state that, on written request within the thirty-day period, the collector will provide the original creditor's name and address if different from the current creditor.
claims.quote: (5) a statement that, upon the consumer's written request within the thirty-day period, the debt collector will provide the consumer with the name and address of the original creditor, if different from the current creditor.

claims.claim: Under subsection (b), written notice within the thirty-day period disputing all or part of the debt triggers a collection pause for the debt or disputed portion.
claims.quote: (b) Disputed debts If the consumer notifies the debt collector in writing within the thirty-day period described in subsection (a) that the debt, or any portion thereof, is disputed, or that the consumer requests the name and address of the original creditor, the debt collector shall cease collection of the debt, or any disputed portion thereof,

claims.claim: A written request within the same period for the original creditor's name and address also triggers the pause.
claims.quote: If the consumer notifies the debt collector in writing within the thirty-day period described in subsection (a) that the debt, or any portion thereof, is disputed, or that the consumer requests the name and address of the original creditor, the debt collector shall cease collection of the debt, or any disputed portion thereof,

claims.claim: The pause lasts until the collector obtains the verification, judgment copy, or original creditor information and mails the corresponding material to the consumer.
claims.quote: until the debt collector obtains verification of the debt or a copy of a judgment, or the name and address of the original creditor, and a copy of such verification or judgment, or name and address of the original creditor, is mailed to the consumer by the debt collector.

claims.claim: Otherwise lawful collection activities and communications may continue during the thirty-day period unless the consumer gives written notice disputing all or part of the debt or requesting the original creditor's name and address.
claims.quote: Collection activities and communications that do not otherwise violate this subchapter may continue during the 30-day period referred to in subsection (a) unless the consumer has notified the debt collector in writing that the debt, or any portion of the debt, is disputed or that the consumer requests the name and address of the original creditor.

claims.claim: Collection during the thirty days may not overshadow or be inconsistent with disclosure of the right to dispute the debt or request the original creditor's name and address.
claims.quote: Any collection activities and communication during the 30-day period may not overshadow or be inconsistent with the disclosure of the consumer's right to dispute the debt or request the name and address of the original creditor.

claims.claim: Under subsection (c), no court may treat failure to dispute the debt as an admission of liability.
claims.quote: (c) Admission of liability The failure of a consumer to dispute the validity of a debt under this section may not be construed by any court as an admission of liability by the consumer.
claims.note: The failure at issue is failure to dispute under this section.

claims.claim: Under subsection (d), a formal pleading in a civil action is not an initial communication for subsection (a).
claims.quote: (d) Legal pleadings A communication in the form of a formal pleading in a civil action shall not be treated as an initial communication for purposes of subsection (a).

claims.claim: California Civil Code section 1788.17 requires every debt collector collecting or attempting to collect a consumer debt to comply with 15 U.S.C. sections 1692b through 1692j, subject to the stated exception.
claims.quote: every debt collector collecting or attempting to collect a consumer debt shall comply with the provisions of Sections 1692b to 1692j, inclusive, of, and shall be subject to the remedies in Section 1692k of, Title 15 of the United States Code.

claims.claim: Section 1788.17 excepts persons specified in section 1692a(6)(A) and (B), or their principal, from section 1692e(11) and section 1692g.
claims.quote: However, subsection (11) of Section 1692e and Section 1692g shall not apply to any person specified in paragraphs (A) and (B) of subsection (6) of Section 1692a of Title 15 of the United States Code or that person’s principal.

claims.claim: Section 1788.17 refers to federal codes as they read on January 1, 2001.
claims.quote: The references to federal codes in this section refer to those codes as they read January 1, 2001.

result.summary: The supplied texts support the claims within the stated scope. The draft reports the 2024 federal text separately from California's January 1, 2001 cross-reference; it does not claim the two federal versions are identical.
